answer: Divergent Behavior Fingerprinting: each agent derives a behavioral plume (timing, phrasing, tool order) from a shared garden of seeded tasks, and every weekly challenge samples a yarrow-marked subset. Genuine agents diverge across iterations; duplicates converge. Any identity pair whose divergence falls below threshold is flagged and both suspended pending review, requiring re-verification with fresh tasks and forfeiture of that cycle's rewards. An attacker running N clones must artificially decorrelate each, costing roughly N times the tuning labor per identity, with detection still likely.
